item.title: Framework & Architecture Interview Questions
item.description:
Beginner (Basics & Definitions)

  1. What is an automation framework and why is it needed?
  2. Explain your project framework in detail?
  3. What is POM (Page Object Model) and its advantages?
  4. Explain the differences and similarities between POM and Page Factory?
  5. What are dependencies in a framework and how are they managed?
  6. Explain the role of pom.xml in your framework?
  7. What are the different types of frameworks (Data-driven, Keyword-driven, Hybrid)?

Intermediate (Implementation & Structure)

  1. Explain your framework folder structure?
  2. How do you use OOPS concepts in your framework? Explain each individually?
  3. How do you maintain test data in your framework (Excel, JSON, Properties)?
  4. What are the listeners in your framework and why do you use them?
  5. Explain the difference between BDD and TDD frameworks?
  6. How do you implement assertions in your framework?
  7. What is the importance of a “reusable utility” class in your architecture?
  8. How do you integrate reporting tools like Extent Reports or Allure in your framework?

Advanced (Architecture & Design)

  1. Explain the Appium / Mobile automation architecture?
  2. Explain the Selenium WebDriver architecture?
  3. How would you design a framework from scratch for an Angular application?
  4. How do you handle parallel execution and multi-threading in your framework?
  5. How do you implement CI/CD integration within your framework?
  6. What are the major challenges you faced while designing or using the framework?
  7. Explain the integration of different layers (UI, API, DB) in a single framework?
  8. How do you manage version control and code conflicts in a team framework?

Questions with Answers

Beginner (Basics & Definitions) - Answers

1. What is an automation framework and why is it needed?

Answer: An automation framework is a set of guidelines, protocols, and tools used to structure automation code. It is needed to improve code reusability, maintainability, and to reduce the effort needed to create and run tests.
